what: Encompass Health runs about 170 inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in the United States, where patients recover after a stroke, a hip replacement or a serious injury before going home.
customers: Patients referred from acute hospitals, paid for mostly by Medicare.
moat: Building a rehabilitation hospital needs state approval in many states, and referral relationships with local acute hospitals take years to build, so each market is hard to enter.
risks: Medicare sets the rates, and a rate decision applies to the whole business at once
Nurse and therapist wages have risen faster than the Medicare rate
opportunities: Revenue grew from $4.0B to $5.9B in four years with a 9.5% net margin
Analysts see about 18% upside, and the company keeps opening new hospitals
The population needing rehabilitation after strokes and joint replacements grows every year
watch: Discharges per hospital and the Medicare rate update each year.
